messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: p99 latency spike >5s for /v1/stream/generate in us-west-2 (streaming path). Alerting on continuous-batching QOS. Auto-escalate to oncall.
jen: On it. checking perf dashboard and recent deploys.
sam: I see a sudden increase in cont-batch tail latency around 17:58 UTC, coincides with packer scheduling jitter. p95 ~600ms -> p99 ~5200ms.
mira: Any customer-facing errors? support-bot, can you surface affected customers?
support-bot: Affected customers: acme-inc (high), beta-ai (low). Acme reports timeouts for streaming sessions. Logged ticket TICKET-4392.
jen: OK. Hypothesis: mixed sequence lengths caused some large batches to stall while waiting for short requests -> KV cache churn + pack refusal.
alex: Can we lower max_batch_size and enable pack-shed temporarily? That usually reduces tail.
sam: Agree. Pushing a config bump to us-west-2 runtime: set batch.max_size=8 -> 4, enable pack_shed=true for streaming queues.
jen: Running the change now. CLI:
```
redwoodctl rollout set-config --region us-west-2 --service streaming-runtime \
  --patch '{"batch.max_size":4,"scheduler.pack_shed":true}'
```
mira: Noted. Adding throttling on background low-priority routes to free slots.
ops-bot: Deploy started: rollout/ci-1755-config/ -> 3 nodes updated.
sam: Quick check of metrics: after config change p95 down to 320ms, p99 down to ~1200ms. Still elevated but much better.
jen: Can we retroactively route heavy long-seq requests to dedicated pool? Use route policy fallback for sequences >1024 to long-seq-pool.
alex: I can flip a routing rule, but need a short maintenance window. If safe, I'll add rule: route(seq_len>1024)->long-seq-pool.
jen: Do it. That will reduce KV contention on streaming path.
alex: Rule applied. Confirmed few long sequences draining to dedicated pool.
mira: Customer impact update: Acme error rate dropped 80%, support notified. Beta-ai saw small improvement.
support-bot: Support message queued to Acme with mitigation steps and ETA for full resolution.
sam: Root cause notes so far: continuous-batching scheduler fairness + mixed sequence lengths created head-of-line blocking. When a long request entered a partial batch, short requests waited -> packer waited -> p99 blow-up.
jen: Action items:
- short: keep batch.max_size=4 and pack_shed=true in us-west-2 for next 2 hours (jen)
- medium: implement seq_len-based fast-path routing to long-seq pool in config (alex)
- medium: add alert for cont-batch tail slope instead of absolute p99 (sam)
- long: explore adaptive batching that splits long sequences or uses multi-queue scheduling (eng-runtime)
mira: I'm on customer comms and will update tickets.
ops-bot: Incident timeline logged to /incidents/1755559999. Tagging docs required.
jen: handing off to night oncall @sam in 20m. If p99 stabilizes <800ms for 30m, we can relax pack_shed.
sam: Acknowledged. I'll monitor dashboards and escalate if reoccur.
alex: Leaving a link to quick rollback if needed: https://runbook/internal/contbatch-rollback
jen: Good work team. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Incident severity changed to SEV2 -> customer-impacting but mitigated.
sam: last check: p95=310ms p99=620ms. Logging final metrics to incident doc and closing live page. Will follow up with postmortem if recurrence.
mira: Copy. Preparing short incident summary for ops-all.
ops-bot: Incident closed from live page at 1755560400.
